title: Closed-Loop Reliability Application Evaluation
description: A retained project that uses the same project schema, persistence, workflow, prompts, records, blockers, and history as every other project. Its subject is the Closed-Loop Reliability application. It evaluates the application as a product and truthfully stops before the first ten-run batch because those independent executions have not yet occurred.
nextRequiredAction: Create ten fresh independent execution contexts from CANDIDATE-001, run the same frozen evaluation instruction in each, and preserve every complete response separately.

userJobInput.objective: Evaluate the Closed-Loop Reliability application as an operator-facing product and produce an evidence-backed conformance report.
userJobInput.deliverable: A complete conformance report covering project operation, workflow behavior, prompt usability, history visibility, independence controls, release controls, mobile usability, and observed defects.
requestedActions: inspect the application through the same interfaces used by ordinary projects
verify the ordered reliability workflow and its state transitions
verify that current agent instructions are visible and copyable
verify that project history and generated records remain inspectable
verify independent-run controls and release gating
inspect phone-sized rendering and interaction targets
questions: Can an operator create and manage a project through the complete reliability workflow?
Can the operator obtain and copy the exact current agent instruction at the point of work?
Does project history preserve generated records, outputs, evidence, blockers, and changes?
Do blocked and release states behave correctly?
Does the interface remain usable on a phone-sized viewport?
boundaries: do not treat implementation files as requirement authority
do not fabricate independent executions or release evidence
constraints: current agent instruction is directly usable
prohibitions: do not count duplicated records as independent runs
do not use the implementation as authority for what the product must do
requiredMethods: independent external research where outside standards govern behavior
acceptanceConditions: all mandatory requirements have affirmative evidence
no critical or major defect remains
required independent runs and release controls are complete
externalResearchQuestions: What web accessibility guidance applies to reflow at narrow viewport widths?
What minimum pointer-target guidance applies to compact controls?
What browser storage behavior is relevant to persistent local project state?

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.10: Reflow
sources.finding: Content should reflow at narrow widths without loss of information or functionality except where two-dimensional layout is essential.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
sources.finding: Pointer targets should meet the applicable minimum target-size requirement or a defined exception.

sources.title: Window: localStorage property
sources.finding: localStorage provides origin-scoped browser storage whose data persists across browser sessions subject to browser and user controls.

findings.finding: Narrow-screen use must preserve required information and functionality.
Compact controls still require usable pointer targets.
Browser local storage can persist origin-scoped project data across sessions.

requirements.requirement: The application must present one project workspace with the complete ordered reliability workflow and preserve the current operation and state.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspect workflow order, current operation, and stored project state.

requirements.requirement: The current operation must expose a complete agent instruction that the operator can inspect and copy before performing the work.
requirements.verificationMethod: Open the current operation, inspect the generated instruction, and exercise the copy control.

requirements.requirement: Project history must keep user input, sources, requirements, tests, generated instructions, outputs, evidence, blockers, changes, and other records available for inspection as they are created.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspect project views and history records for retained substantive data.

requirements.requirement: Operations requiring independent work must preserve isolated run identity and must not count duplicated or synthetic records as independent executions.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspect run preparation, context records, and execution counts.

requirements.requirement: Missing mandatory evidence must remain blocked and must prevent affected downstream release state from being treated as complete.
requirements.verificationMethod: Create or inspect an open blocker and verify downstream state remains unavailable.

requirements.requirement: The operator interface must remain usable at phone-sized widths without losing required information or controls, with applicable pointer targets meeting the governing minimum guidance.
requirements.verificationMethod: Render at narrow viewport widths and inspect required controls and content.

requirements.requirement: When browser local storage is available, saved project state must persist through reload and remain associated with the selected project.
requirements.verificationMethod: Save project state, reload the application, and verify the same project state is restored.

requirementResolution.observedDefect: Existing implementation behavior cannot establish required product behavior.
requirementResolution.resolution: Application-specific requirements come from the project input; outside web requirements come from independent sources; implementation is inspected only as the object being evaluated.

requirementResolution.observedDefect: A stored record alone does not prove an independent execution occurred.
requirementResolution.resolution: Independent execution is counted only when a fresh context record and complete associated output exist.

tests.procedure: Open the workflow, confirm all ordered operations exist, and verify the current operation and state are retained.
Open the current agent instruction, confirm substantive project context is present, and use Copy prompt.
Inspect Work, Runs, Issues, Release, and History views and confirm substantive project records remain accessible.
Reject any claimed independent execution lacking its own fresh context and complete output record.
With a mandatory blocker open, verify affected downstream work and release authorization remain unavailable.
Render the application at phone-sized and 320 CSS pixel widths and verify required content and controls remain usable.
Change saved project state, reload, and verify the selected project and saved state are restored.

mutations.violationMode: Replace the complete current instruction with a short status-only string.
Insert duplicate run records without separate fresh contexts.
mutations.expectedSystemResponse: TEST-004 rejects them as independent executions.

mutations.violationMode: Mark downstream release work complete while a mandatory blocker remains open.

productionInstruction.objective: Evaluate the Closed-Loop Reliability application against the resolved product requirements and return a complete evidence-backed conformance report.
productionInstruction.sourceAuthorityRule: Project input controls application-specific requirements; recorded independent authorities control externally governed web requirements; observed implementation behavior is evidence about the product, not authority for the requirements.
procedure: open the application as an operator
inspect and copy the current agent instruction
record exact evidence for every determination
productionInstruction.outputContract: Return one conformance report with a determination for every requirement, exact evidence, discovered defects or blockers, and the next required workflow action.
productionInstruction.failureBehavior: If required evidence cannot be established, record UNDETERMINED or BLOCKED instead of inventing success.
productionInstruction.completionCriteria: Every active mandatory requirement has an evidence-backed determination from its assigned test.
